title: Jagmohan Singh vs Bachan Singh on 28 April, 2026
full_text: Jagmohan Singh vs Bachan Singh on 28 April, 2026 IN THE COURT OF Ms. AASTHA SHARMA, LD. JMFC (N.I. Act)-03, SOUTH-EAST DISTRICT, SAKET COURTS COMPLEX: DELHI Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh CC No. 2784/2018 U/S 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 1. CNR number DLSE020097192018 2. Name of the complainant Sh. Jagmohan Singh, S/o Sh. Preet Singh, R/o E-350, G.K. - II, New Delhi. 3. Name of the accused person(s), parentage Sh. Bachan Singh, & residential address S/o Sh. Sarni Singh, R/o C -17, FF, New Friends Colony, East, New Delhi - 110065. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 1 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.04.28 16:01:14 +0530 4. Offence complained of or proved U/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 5. Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty and claimed trial 6. Final Judgment/order Acquitted 7. Date of judgment/order 28.04.2026. Date of Institution : 02.04.2018 Date of Reserving Judgment/Order : 14.03.2026 Date of Pronouncement of Judgment/Order : 28.04.2026 ARGUING COUNSELS: Ld. Counsel for the complainant : Sh. Sanjay Kumar Sharma Ld. Counsel for the Accused : Sh. Surendra Kumar Roy Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:20 +0530 CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 2 of 14 JUDGMENT 1. Vide this judgment, this Court shall dispose of the present complaint filed by the complainant Sh. Jagmohan Singh (hereinafter referred to as "complainant") against Sh. Bachan Singh (hereinafter "accused") under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 read with Section 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as " NI Act "). Brief facts of the case: 2. It is the case of the complainant, A. That, the complainant and the accused were known to each other since very long and the accused approached the complainant for a friendly loan of Rs. 4,00,000/-, which the complainant agreed to considering their friendly relations. That, the complainant advanced the sum of Rs. 4,00,000/- in the month of August 2016 for a period of one month. That, in order to discharge his existing liability, the accused issued a cheque bearing no. 829711 dated 29.01.2018 in the sum of Rs. 4,00,000/-, drawn on IndusInd Bank, Gurgaon Branch, Haryana in favour of the complainant. B. That, on presentation of the aforesaid cheques in question by the complainant with his banker ICICI Bank Ltd., Greater Kailash, New Delhi, the cheque was dishonoured with the remarks "Payment Stopped by Drawer" vide return memo dated 31.01.2018. C. In these circumstances, the complainant got issued a statutory legal demand notice to the accused through his counsel, dated 13.02.2018, thereby requiring the CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 3 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:24 +0530 accused to pay the amount of the aforesaid cheques within a period of 15 days from the receipt of the said notice. The said notice under Sec. 138 of NI Act was sent to the accused through Registered AD/Speed Post/Courier at his correct address on 15.02.2018 and 19.02.2018 respectively. That despite service of the above stated notice of demand, the Accused has deliberately and willfully failed to comply with the said notice of demand and has failed to pay the amount of the aforesaid cheque within the stipulated period of 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice. Consequently, this case was filed by the complainant against the accused, which was within the limitation period as laid down u/s 138 , NI Act. 3. In the pre-summoning evidence, the complainant examined himself on affidavit being Ex. CW1/G and placed on record Cheque in question Ex. CW-1/A; Bank Return memos Ex. CW-1/B; Copy of legal demand notice and postal receipt Ex. CW-1/C & Ex. CW-1/D and Tracking Report Ex. CW-1/E (Colly.). 4. Upon prima facie consideration of the pre-summoning evidence, the accused person was summoned. 5. Upon the appearance of the accused, notice under Section 251 CrPC was served upon him on 07.02.2019 to which he pleaded not guilty. The accused has accepted issuance of cheque in favour of the complainant and also his signatures on the cheque in question. The accused has denied receiving the legal demand notice. The accused has stated that he had issued the cheque in question as a security cheque to the complainant and he had already made the payment towards the cheque in question to the complainant partly by way of bank transfer and partly by way of transfer. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 4 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:28 +0530 6. CW-1, CW-2 and CW-3 were examined-in-chief, cross-examined and discharged. Thereby, CE was closed on 19.03.2025. Accordingly, matter proceeded to the stage of recording the statement of the accused. 7. Statement of accused under Section 313 CrPC read with Section 281 CrPC was recorded on 10.09.2025 wherein the accused opted to lead defence evidence. However, later the Ld. Counsel for the accused on behalf of the accused submitted that they do not wish to lead DE and therefore, vide order of this court, DE was closed by recording a separate statement of the Ld. Counsel for the accused. 8. Thereafter, the matter was listed for final arguments. After hearing the final arguments from both sides, the matter was reserved for pronouncement of judgment. 9. It is well settled position of law that to constitute an offence under Section 138 , NI Act, the following ingredients are required to be fulfilled: I. drawing of the cheque by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker, II. The cheque was issued for payment to another person for discharge in whole/part any debt or liability; III. Cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier. RBI in its notification DBOD.AML BC.No.47/14.01.001/2011-12 has reduced the aforesaid period from 6 months to 3 months. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 5 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:32 +0530 IV. Returning of the cheque unpaid by the drawee bank for want of sufficient funds to the credit of the drawer or any arrangement with the banker to pay the sum covered by the cheque; V. Giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 30 days of the receipt of information by the payee from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid demanding payment of the cheque amount; VI. Failure of the drawer to make payment to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, of the amount covered by the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the notice. The offence under Section 138 , NI Act is made out against the drawer of the cheque, only when all the aforementioned ingredients are fulfilled. 10. Analysing all the concerned provisions of law and various pronouncements in this regard, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Basalingappa v. Mudibasappa [AIR 2019 SC 1983] held that: I. Once the execution of cheque is admitted, Section 139 of the Act mandates that a presumption be drawn that the cheque in question was for the discharge of any debt or other liability. II. The presumption under Section 139 is a rebuttable presumption and the onus is on the accused to raise the probable defence. The standard of proof for rebutting the presumption is that of preponderance of probabilities. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 6 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:37 +0530 III. To rebut the presumption, it is open for the accused to rely on evidence led by him or accused can also rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise a probable defence. Inference of preponderance of probabilities can be drawn not only from the materials brought on record by reference to the circumstances upon which they rely. IV. That it is not necessary for the accused to come in the witness box in support of his defence. Section 139 imposes an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden. It is therefore implied that the law regarding the presumption for the offence under Section 138 , NI Act, the presumptions under Section 118(a) and Section 139 have to be compulsorily raised as soon as the execution of cheque by the accused is admitted or proved by the complainant and thereafter the burden is shifted upon the accused to prove otherwise. Appreciation of evidence and marshalling of facts: 11. Issuance of cheque: The complainant has filed on record the original cheques, i.e., bearing no. 829711 dated 29.01.2018 for Rs. 4,00,000/- drawn on IndusInd Bank, Gurgaon (Ex. CW1/A). In notice under Section 251 CrPC, the accused has admitted that the cheque in dispute belongs to him. It is also not disputed that the cheque in question is not drawn on the account maintained by the accused person and it is impliedly admitted therefore that the accused is the drawer of the cheque. Therefore, ingredient number I stands fulfilled in the present case. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 7 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.04.28 16:01:43 +0530 12. Presentment and dishonor of cheque: As per the RBI guidelines, it is essential for the cheque in question be to presented within a period of three months from the date on which they are drawn and the same be returned as unpaid by the drawee bank for want of sufficient funds to the credit of the drawer or any arrangement with the banker to pay the sum covered by the cheque. In the case at hand, the cheque in question was returned vide return memo dated 31.01.2018 (Ex. CW1/B) due to the reason "Payment Stopped by Drawer" By implication thereof, the cheque was presented within three months and the same was returned. Therefore, Ingredient number III & IV stand fulfilled in the present case. 13. Legal demand notice and payment by the accused thereof: The legal notice dated 13.02.2018 (Ex. CW1/C) was dispatched on 13.02.2018 vide Speed Post (Ex. CW1/D) (Colly.), i.e., within 30 days of return of the bank memo indicating cheques in question being unpaid. The fact that the legal demand notice has made a clear and unambiguous demand for payment of the cheque in question is not disputed. The accused has not accepted the receiving of legal demand notice in notice u/s 251 CrPC. However, as per the presumption raised under Section 114 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and Section 27 of General Clauses Act, if the legal demand notice is sent at the correct address, then the same shall be deemed to have been duly served, as per the precedent laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in C.C. Alavi Haji v. Palapetty Muhammed , (2007) 3 SCC (Cri). The ingredient number V is fulfilled by virtue of giving of legal demand notice within 30 days from the bank return memo. The receipt of legal demand notice by the accused is deemed to be admitted as per the discussion above. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 8 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.04.28 16:01:48 +0530 14. Moving on, it is not disputed that the accused has not made the payment of the cheque amount within 15 days of the receipt of legal demand notice. Therefore, ingredient number VI also stands fulfilled in the present case. Presumption under Section 118A read with Section 139 , NI Act 15. The NI Act raises two presumptions in favour of the holder of the cheque, i.e., complainant; firstly, with regard to the issuance of cheque for consideration, as contained in Section 118(a) and secondly, with regard to the fact that the holder of cheque received the same for discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, as contained in Section 139 of the Act. These presumptions shall end only when the contrary is proved by the accused, that is, the cheque was not issued for consideration and in discharge of any debt or liability etc. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment titled Rangappa Vs. Sri Mohan , (2010) 11 SCC 441 held that a reverse onus clause usually imposes an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden and when an accused has to rebut the presumption under Section 139 , the standard of proof for doing so is that of "preponderance of probabilities". Therefore, if the accused is able to raise a probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability, the prosecution can fail. It was further held that the accused can rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise such a defence and it is conceivable that in some cases the accused may not need to adduce evidence of his/her own. Once a probable defence is raised, then the onus is shifted to the complainant to establish that a legally enforceable liability existed in his favour and CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 9 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:53 +0530 the burden of proof on the complainant in this case is that of "beyond reasonable doubt." 16. The accused can rebut the presumption as raised under Section 138 , NI Act by: (a) putting forth his defence at the time of framing of notice u/s 251 CrPC; (b) cross-examining the complainant; (c) when statement of accused is recorded u/s 313 CrPC; (d) or by leading defence evidence, thereby demolishing the case of the complainant. Rebuttal of Presumption by Accused as to existence of legally enforceable debt 17. In light of the above discussion, since the accused has admitted to issuance of cheques, admitted the signatures on the cheques and legal notice has also been deemed to be served, what is left to be seen is whether the accused has been able to rebut the presumption against him, i.e., whether the accused is able to raise a probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt? 18. In the present case, in order to discharge his initial burden to prove the abovementioned ingredients, the complainant relied upon the affidavit of the complainant being Ex. CW1/G and placed on record documents mentioned hereinbefore. The case of the complainant is that the accused had issued the cheque CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 10 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.04.28 16:01:58 +0530 in question in discharge of his liability qua the loan taken from the complainant and the accused has admitted to the loan in question as well. The accused has taken a consistent defence and has stated that he had repaid the liability owed by him to the complainant partly by way of bank transfer and partly by cash and the accused has indicated certain payments towards the complainant by account transfer by relying upon the statement of account of the complainant, i.e., Mark CW1/AB. Further, the complainant has admitted to certain transactions being made by the accused to the complainant and has stated as follows: "...Before presenting the cheque in question, I had received some money from the accused but I do not remember the exact amount but the amount given was not in lieu of principal amount. I had given an interest free loan to the accused...." "....I have not annexed any document which shows how much amount I had received from the accused in my bank account but I can produce the same on NDOH." "...Accused has paid me Rs. 1,43,000/- to me but Rs. 1,43,000/- was paid in the form of profit as well as late payment and the principal amount of Rs. 4,00,000/- will pay together in future. It is correct that no agreement was executed regarding interest. It is correct that loan was interest free. So I do not mention in my legal notice/complaint and evidence but it was agreed between both of us that accused will pay certain amount as compensation or as got profited from the said amount invested in the business to the complainant..." CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 11 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.04.28 16:02:05 +0530 "...The accused has paid Rs. 1,43,000/- in the year 2017-2018.." On one hand, the complainant is stating that the loan advanced to the accused was interest-free in nature and on the other hand, the complainant is stating that the sum of Rs. 1,43,000/- received by the complainant from the accused was qua interest/compensation in lieu of principal amount not being repaid in time. 19. The complainant has neither endorsed the amount of Rs. 1,43,000/- on the cheque in question nor placed on record any document to indicate that interest/compensation was to be paid by the accused to the complainant. The accused had already rebutted his liability to the tune of the amount mentioned in the cheque in question, when the complainant admitted to receiving a certain amount from the accused and the onus of proof has shifted upon the complainant to prove that the accused owed the liability as stated by the complainant in her cheque in question. 20. In the present case, the complainant has failed to place anything on record to indicate the liability of the accused on the date of the presentation of the cheque in question. The accused, however, has placed on record proof of payment to rebut the presumption that the accused owes the liability as mentioned on the cheque in question. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Dashrathbhai Trikambhai Patel v. Hitesh M. Patel (2023) 1 SCC 578 has held that "for the commission of offence u/s 138 NI Act, the cheque that is dishonoured must represent a legally enforceable debt on the date of maturity or presentation." The complainant failed to discharge the onus and no evidence was produced to show the actual liability of the accused on the date of presentation of the cheque in question. Moreover the complainant has not CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 12 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.04.28 16:02:10 +0530 even mentioned about the repayment by the accused in the legal demand notice as well as in the evidence by way of affidavit. 21. The accused therefore has rebutted the presumption u/s 139 NI Act by proving that the liability of the accused is lesser than what has been stated by the complainant in the cheque in question, as certain payment has been made by the accused towards the liability. While, the complainant has been unsuccessful in proving that the accused owed the liability as stated in the cheque in question, despite the payment made by the accused as depicted by Mark CW1/AB by placing on record any document to indicate the liability of the accused on the date of presentation of the cheque in question. 22. In view of the aforesaid findings and analysis, this court has arrived at an irresistible conclusion that the accused has been able to cast a shadow of reasonable doubt upon the case of the complainant by rebutting the mandatory presumption resting in its favour and by several inconsistencies in the version of the complainant. Once the accused had created a probable defence as to the legally enforceable liability, the onus shifted on the complainant to prove the existence of legally enforceable liability of the accused, as on the date of the drawal or presentation of the impugned cheques, which has not been fulfilled by the complainant in the present case. Since this basic ingredient which is pivotal to attract liability under Section 138 NI Act has not been proved by the complainant, accordingly, no offence of dishonour of the impugned cheque under the said Section is made out. 23. In light of the discussion above, ingredient no. II has not been fulfilled in the present case. CC No. 2784/2018 Jagmohan Singh Vs. Bachan Singh Page 13 of 14 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.04.28 16:02:14 +0530 Conclusion: 24. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the accused Bachan Singh has been successful in establishing a probable defence on a standard of preponderance of probabilities to rebut the presumption under Section 118 and 139 of the NI Act by punching holes in the case of the complainant and making the case of the complainant doubtful. The accused has been successful in establishing a probable defence and as a consequence, questioning the existence of legally enforceable liability in favour of the complainant and that the cheque was not issued by the accused in discharge of existing legally enforceable debt or liability owed to the complainant. In the result of the analysis of the present case, the accused Bachan Singh is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 138 , Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. PRONOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT TODAY Digitally signed by AASTHA th AASTHA SHARMA ON 28 April, 2026.
